results.summary: This design displays the letter P on a seven-segment display when a correct secret code is entered on the input switches. It is a first Tiny Tapeout chip built in Wokwi, with four input pins and four output pins. Testing is done by trying different DIP switch positions to find the code. The documentation deliberately withholds the code logic, so the exact behaviour cannot be verified from the text.

This design uses a clock and a button input, and requires external hardware to generate current, a button, and something to display the outputs. The documentation is thin and the design is explicitly labelled broken, so its intended behaviour is unclear.

This design checks eight switches arranged in pairs and lights a seven-segment display with a zero only when exactly one pair is on. Testing is done by manually flipping switches in the Wokwi online project, and the seven-segment display from the template is the only external hardware.
The documentation is very brief and does not describe the decoding logic in detail.
This project is a first Wokwi design described as a logic circuit test for the Wokwi platform.

This project implements a full adder and full subtractor with two 4-bit registers, selecting the operation and destination register via control inputs. Data is entered in binary on four input pins, the register is chosen with one input, and add or subtract is chosen with another.
This design combines a mutex arbiter, an inefficient C-gate, and an LFSR that drives a 4-bit pseudo-random output. The documentation does not specify any external hardware.
